scope: Read-only specification audit of docs/specs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-product.md against the explicit user intent and workflow in .pipeline/context.md and AGENTS.md, using the audit-spec skill. Migration and current-contract assertions were checked against legacy README.md, config.example.toml, install.sh, and the argv/worker/register code paths in the `ptest` script at the worktree's base commit. Judged as a product contract; detailed design choices deliberately left open were not demanded.
coverage: Checked: coherence across sections 1-13; missing material behaviors (uninitialized repo, cancellation trigger, nested invocations, runner cwd, guide location); finite scope and milestone/acceptance mapping (A1-A14 vs M2-M4); state/failure/cancellation/invalidation rows in sections 4-5 and the fallback table; security/resource boundaries in sections 6, 7, 10; migration declarations in P4 versus the legacy CLI (register at ptest:2624, --local/--fresh at ptest:2743-2748, shell-evaluated config commands at ptest:2811-2815, worker flag stripping at ptest:272-326, worktree common-dir resolution at ptest:211-238, atomic installer switch in install.sh:16-20, exit codes 2/75 in README.md:344-361); interoperability claims versus docs/research/2026-09-17-agent-interoperability.md; performance targets for measurability and honesty. Not checked: no tests, benchmarks, or commands were executed; no native TUI integration was exercised or verified; the provisional cx-ng-foundation tree and the historical cloud proposal at /home/ingmar/code/persea_content_maker/ptest_ng.md were not read because the brief directs judgment against user intent rather than those artifacts; .pipeline/out/runtime-preflight.json and the Muse preflight traces were not opened. Findings about runner-specific flag behavior (xdist, Vitest config precedence) are deferred to design as the spec itself states.

blocking.issue: The admission domain identity is defined in a way that both permits silent evasion and provides no sanctioned isolation for the project's own subprocess fixtures.
blocking.location: docs/specs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-product.md section 4 S1 (line 104), section 3 P2 machine-local settings (line 88), section 11 intro and A2 (lines 269, 274); AGENTS.md line 8
blocking.evidence: S1: 'cooperates with other invocations under the same host/OS-user and resolved scheduler configuration ... A repo config cannot create a private domain to evade the shared limit.' P2: 'Machine-local settings own the shared host budget, private state location, and optional local overrides.' If the private state location is part of 'resolved scheduler configuration', an invocation launched by a TUI or shell with a different env/config path resolves a different location and forms a second domain with its own full budget, so two agent sessions on one host run 2x the ceiling without any repo config change; that contradicts 'Coordination spans repositories, Git worktrees, shells, and TUIs.' Conversely, if no such override exists, the spec's own acceptance evidence cannot run: AGENTS.md line 8 requires all tests through ptest, section 11 says 'Deterministic tests run through ptest', and A2 starts six ptest subprocesses with budget 1 (A3/A4 spawn more) inside the same host/user domain. The outer ptest run holds the single grant; the six inner fixtures queue behind it until the configured queue deadline and the test fails with exit 75. The spec sanctions neither an explicit fixture domain nor a nested-invocation behavior.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: The user requires cooperation across simultaneous agent sessions, repos and worktrees, and the acceptance priorities require fair admission proven by real subprocess tests. As written the domain contract is either evadable by ordinary environment differences or makes A2-A4 unexecutable under the mandated ptest-only test workflow, so the scheduler contract is not consistently testable.
blocking.fix: Define the v1 admission domain key as host + OS user resolved from a single default private state root that per-invocation environment cannot silently change. Allow exactly one explicit alternate-domain mechanism (a named machine-local setting or flag) whose use is printed by `where`, `status`, and every plan/result artifact as 'isolated domain', intended for containers and test fixtures. Add a nested-invocation rule: a ptest started as a descendant of an admitted run must either run in an explicitly declared fixture domain or receive a documented immediate outcome (for example exit 75 with a nested-invocation reason) rather than waiting to deadline. Add the corresponding negative case to A2/A4: an env-only difference cannot create a second domain.

blocking.issue: Exit semantics for an explicit `ptest --full` that passes while relevant files change during the run are contradictory between T3 and C3, and 'relevant' is not bounded against writes the run itself produces.
blocking.location: docs/specs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-product.md section 5 T3 (line 140) versus section 8 C3 (line 232); section 5 T3 ignored-content paragraph (line 138)
blocking.evidence: T3: 'If relevant files change during execution, label the result as a changed-during-run observation, retain its actual failures, and publish no baseline/full-gate evidence for the final tree.' C3: 'A successful child may still produce a nonzero ptest operational status when ptest cannot validate required automatic-run/full-gate evidence, including a relevant source change during a full gate.' Scenario: an agent runs `ptest --full` and the configured full command is `vitest run -u` or a pytest suite that rewrites a tracked golden file, or an editor formatter saves a file mid-run. All tests pass. Under T3 the process exits 0 with an artifact that says not full-gate eligible; an agent reading only exit status treats the tree as verified. Under C3 the process exits nonzero (70) on a green run; agents learn to distrust ptest failures. Because line 138 says ignored generated/runtime inputs are fingerprinted, a naive implementation would also flag `.coverage`, `.pytest_cache`, or snapshot writes produced by the run, so the nonzero path can fire on every ordinary full gate.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: The brief requires preserving runner exit status and the acceptance list (A11) forbids a false `passed` status; the spec must give one answer that implementers and agents can rely on, and must not let the run's own artifacts invalidate the gate.
blocking.fix: State one semantic in both T3 and C3 for explicit `--full` with a changed-during-run tree (recommended: preserve the runner's exit code for the process, mark `full_gate_eligible: false` with reason in the artifact and a prominent stderr line, and reserve nonzero operational status for automatic mode). Define that writes to paths owned by the run (declared runner artifacts, coverage data, caches, snapshot updates requested by the effective command's own options) are not 'relevant source changes'; anything else that changed is disclosed by path class in the artifact. Add an A5/A11 case: a passing full gate whose run writes its own artifacts remains passed and baseline-eligible, while an external tracked-file edit mid-run yields the chosen status.

blocking.issue: The Exposure axis promises that credentials in argv never enter diagnostics, history, prompts, or JSON, but ptest cannot identify arbitrary secret argv values, and other sections require the effective command to be inspectable. The negative evidence as written is unimplementable and dishonest as an absolute claim.
blocking.location: docs/specs/2026-09-17-ptest-ng-product.md section 10 Exposure row (line 259); section 8 C1 (line 224); section 4 S3 status (line 112); section 8 history/status rows (lines 216, 219)
blocking.evidence: Line 259: 'Dotenv, credentials in env/URLs/argv, source snippets, and unrelated filesystem contents do not enter ptest diagnostics/history/prompts/JSON.' Line 224: 'the effective command/capability is inspectable without leaking secret option values.' Line 112: `ptest status` exposes state 'without publishing ... raw secret-bearing commands.' Scenario: a committed `.ptest.toml` or a user invocation contains `--database-url postgres://app:s3cret@db/test` or `--api-token abc`; `ptest where`, `status`, `history`, and the result artifact must show the effective argv per C1 and section 8. No rule in the spec tells ptest which values are secret, so either the argv is shown (violating line 259) or ptest must guess (untestable). The same row correctly says raw runner streams are not secret-filtered, so the spec already acknowledges the limit for one channel but not the other.
blocking.whyItFailsDoD: Section 10 requires every axis to have testable negative regression evidence and the acceptance priorities require honest claims; an absolute promise with no defined redaction policy cannot be turned into a fixture and would mislead users reading the security documentation.
blocking.fix: Replace the absolute argv/URL claim with a defined policy: environment values are never stored; URL userinfo and values of a documented option-name deny-list (password/token/secret/key style names, extendable via config) are redacted in every ptest-owned output; all other argv is displayed as configured, and the documentation states that secrets belong in env or files, not argv. Keep the 'raw runner streams are not filtered' residual. Add the corresponding A11/A8 negative fixture: a URL with userinfo and a deny-listed option in config and on the command line are redacted in `where`, `status`, `history`, JSON, and prompts, while the child still receives the literal values.

notes: Migration declarations (P4, lines 96-100) omit legacy behaviors that change: bare `ptest`, `ptest .`, and whole-suite directories are refused today as 'full in disguise' (ptest:2764-2780) but become automatic or explicit scoped runs; `ptest status` exits 1 when attention is needed today (README.md:32) but section 8 says inspection exits 0; unregistered repos auto-detect and run today (ptest:252, 2755) whereas the spec implies init is required but never states the uninitialized-repository outcome; `also_roots` becomes obsolete under repo-local config. Add these to the migration preview text so existing repository instructions and agent habits can be updated.

Cancellation is described (S4, A3) but its trigger is never named: SIGINT/SIGTERM to the invoking ptest process, TUI abort of the process group, or a command. The CLI table has no cancel/reclaim verb, so a run whose parent was SIGKILLed by a TUI leaves a live orphan that holds capacity until it exits; the only remedy is a manual kill followed by the 30-second recovery. State the trigger explicitly and say whether an owner-scoped `ptest cancel <run>` is in v1 or deferred.

The working directory of the child runner is not stated. Legacy always runs the configured command with cwd = resolved git root (ptest:2754, run_local). Under 'literal argv', a path argument typed from a subdirectory is interpreted by the runner relative to whatever cwd ptest chooses. One sentence in C1 declaring child cwd = project root (or invocation cwd) removes an avoidable ambiguity.

Section 9 requires 'one generic repository guide' and 'thin pointers' from native entry files, while init only prints snippets by default. State where the guide lives (installed with ptest and printable via a command/`--help` section, or optionally written into the repo on explicit request) so a pointer in a user's AGENTS.md has a stable target; the research proposed docs/ptest-agent.md in the user repo, which init does not create.

The config model implies exactly one runner per `.ptest.toml` and uses nested configurations for multi-project repos (line 90). Make that explicit so a single-root repo containing both pytest and Vitest knows to use nested configs and that `ptest --full` at the ambiguous root reports ambiguity rather than picking one.

Doctor's 2,000-file / 16 MiB static budget (line 173) is phrased as a ceiling. Ordinary mid-size repositories exceed 2,000 files, so doctor would routinely terminate early; state that test, conftest, fixture, and setup files are inspected first within the budget and whether an explicit higher budget is permitted, or doctor's usefulness on real repos is limited by design.

Arbitrary-command support (line 71) reserves the entire configured capacity exclusively even when the user supplies a bounded wrapper. A declared reservation (user-attested worker count) would fit S2's explicit accounting; this is a preference, not a defect.

A full run that passes all tests but fails its coverage threshold exits nonzero and therefore never becomes a baseline (T3 'successful full run'); a repository under its coverage floor can never narrow. This is consistent with preserving gates; say it explicitly so it is not read as a bug later.

Side-by-side migration: the installed legacy bundle does not participate in the NG admission domain, so legacy runs in flight are invisible to NG budgets until the live CLI is replaced. Worth one sentence in P1/P4 and the migration guide.

Verified against the legacy code: `register` (ptest:2624), `--local`/`--fresh` parsing (ptest:2743-2748), shell-evaluated config commands with quoted passthrough (ptest:2811-2815), worker-flag stripping/insertion (ptest:272-396), common-dir worktree resolution (ptest:211-238), the atomic installer switch (install.sh:16-20), and exit codes 2/75 (README.md:344-361) all match the spec's assertions. The interoperability section matches the research document, including the single Muse loading smoke.
